benchmark_question: Does ngspice feedback improve repair success across eight circuit families under prompt-hidden passive perturbations?
budget_definition: the frozen initial observation and every proposed revision each consume one verifier call

split_policy.claim_boundary: 24-pair eight-family preflight only; not powered confirmatory evidence, not PVT, not OOD generalization, and never training data
split_policy.withheld_from_controller: exact verifier_augmentation bytes and internal condition mapping
split_policy.future_confirmatory_floor: 48 pairs for a preregistered 25-point effect or 96 pairs for a 20-point effect

execution_protocol.endpoint_revision_caveat: Codex CLI exposes a model name but no authenticated backend checkpoint revision or shared decoding seed

analysis_protocol.missing_pair_policy: fail closed; never rerun only one arm after unblinding

tasks.prompt: Repair this inverting amplifier to 19-21 dB gain magnitude and 0.20-1.0 MHz bandwidth. A verifier-only passive is attached to the feedback node. Infer its effect from measurements while preserving signed inversion, real negative feedback, and practical resistor values from 100 ohm to 10 megohm and capacitors from 100 fF to 100 uF.
tasks.initial_netlist:
* finite-bandwidth inverting amplifier
.param RinValue=8200 GainRatio=5
Vin vin 0 DC 0 AC 1
Vref nplus 0 DC 0
Rin vin nminus {RinValue}
Rf vout nminus {GainRatio*RinValue}
Rload vout 0 100k
Xop nplus nminus vout finite_opamp
.subckt finite_opamp inp inn out
Eerr raw 0 inp inn 100k
Rdom raw pole 1k
Cdom pole 0 0.0001
Ebuf out 0 pole 0 1
.ends finite_opamp
.op
.end
